record.paper_title: Some Open Problems on Multiple Ergodic Averages
record.original_question: Consider the random increasing sequence a_n(ω) obtained by selecting each integer n independently with probability σ_n, where nσ_n → ∞. Almost surely, is this random sequence good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence for commuting transformations? Equivalently, for every commuting system (X, X, μ, T1, ..., Tℓ) and bounded measurable f1, ..., fℓ, do the random averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T1^{a_n(ω)}f1 · ... · Tℓ^{a_n(ω)}fℓ converge in L^2 to the same limit as the deterministic averages along n?

evidence.quote: Problem 31. Suppose that nσn → ∞. Show that almost surely the sequence (an(ω)) is good for multiple recurrence and convergence of commuting transformations. Moreover, show that almost surely the following holds: For every system (X, X , µ, T1, . . . , T`) and functions f1, . . . , f` ∈ L∞(µ), the averages (1/N) ΣN n=1 T1^an(ω) f1 · · · T`^an(ω) f` converge in L^2(µ) and their limit equals the limit of the averages (1/N) ΣN n=1 T1^n f1 · · · T`^n f`.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(\sigma_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ be a sequence of real numbers with $0\le\sigma_n\le 1$ satisfying $n\sigma_n\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$. Construct a random increasing sequence of positive integers $(a_n(\omega))$ as follows: independently for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$, include $n$ in the sequence with probability $\sigma_n$, and let $a_1(\omega)<a_2(\omega)<\cdots$ be the enumeration of the chosen integers (this is well defined almost surely since $\sum\sigma_n=\infty$).

Prove or disprove: almost surely, the sequence $(a_n(\omega))$ is good for multiple recurrence and multiple convergence with respect to commuting measure-preserving transformations. Precisely, show that almost surely the following holds. For every $\ell\in\mathbb{N}$, every probability space $(X,\mathcal{X},\mu)$ equipped with commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations $T_1,\dots,T_\ell$, and all functions $f_1,\dots,f_\ell\in L^\infty(\mu)$, the averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} (T_1^{a_n(\omega)}f_1)\cdots(T_\ell^{a_n(\omega)}f_\ell)$$
converge in $L^2(\mu)$ as $N\to\infty$, and the limit equals the $L^2$-limit of the deterministic averages
$$\frac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N} (T_1^{n}f_1)\cdots(T_\ell^{n}f_\ell).$$
artifact.category_tag: multiple ergodic averages along random sequences
artifact.status_search_result: Existing literature (Frantzikinakis–Lesigne–Wierdl and related works) establishes random multiple recurrence/convergence results in restricted settings — e.g. powers of a single transformation, or two commuting transformations under specific decay assumptions on σ_n such as σ_n = n^{-a} with a in a small range. No source found resolves the full problem for arbitrary ℓ commuting transformations under only the hypothesis nσ_n → ∞; the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Random Sequences and Pointwise Convergence of Multiple Ergodic Averages
status_evidence.snippet: Pointwise convergence is proved for averages (1/N)Σ f(T^n x) g(S^{a_n} x) where a_n is a random version of [n^c], in restricted settings.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial results are known for commuting transformations along random sequences, restricted to two transformations and specific σ_n.

status_evidence.title: Multiple recurrence and convergence without commutativity
status_evidence.snippet: Frantzikinakis (2023) addresses multiple recurrence/convergence results in further special settings.
status_evidence.claim: Recent works continue to address restricted versions, indicating the general problem remains open.
